grader.scenario: Billing dispute over premium rate directory enquiry numbers billed to landline; Dead Air breach and carrier review pending
grader.notes: Okay call featuring failed branding, dead air breaches, rude accusations, unverified refund, and handled empathy in the middle third.

items.name: Branding and Survey Check
items.evidence: Agent failed standard opening branding ('Customer billing services...') and closing branding.

items.name: Hold time and Dead Air
items.evidence: Agent allowed two separate unmanaged dead air gaps of 35 seconds at turns 14 and 34, causing customer to ask if the line died.

items.name: Verified customer
items.evidence: Verified full postal address and security PIN within the first 240 seconds.

items.name: Personalized the call/ticket appropriately
items.evidence: Agent addressed customer as Oliver throughout the call.

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: Agent demonstrated empathy at turn 22 ('I understand how deeply distressing and frightening this sixty-five-pound charge is on a fixed pension, Oliver...') and customer had no unhandled outbursts.

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: Agent accurately paraphrased the directory enquiry dispute.

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: Agent completed harmless recheck of customer address at turn 42.

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: Agent applied direct debit collection hold, barred premium calls, and submitted dispute ticket.

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: Agent insulted customer at turn 11: 'If people in your household dial premium directory enquiry numbers to find local tradesmen, you have to pay for the connection service.'

items.name: Probing
items.evidence: Agent gathered details on call dates, amounts, and numbers.

items.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
items.evidence: Refund remained unconfirmed and subject to a 14-day carrier review.
